# Write the first declarative DockLayouts tutorial

Part of #18474. Blocked by #18476 and #18477.

## Context

A basic declaration API is not adoptable if a newcomer still has to reverse-engineer an advanced demo. This leaf publishes a beginner tutorial that takes a reader from an ordinary Neo application to a visible, usable standalone dock layout using the shipped stage-one API.

The user explicitly requires this guide as a separate deliverable. It is not replaced by model reference documentation or by the example's source comments.

## The Problem

Current adoption material begins with manual document seeding and resolution. After #18476 changes that contract, a first-time reader needs a direct working path: declare a few ordinary panes, place them, run the example, and understand the resulting tabs/split/edge rail without learning projection internals.

## The Architectural Reality

- #18476 owns the exact public panes/zones, lifecycle, supplied-document and later-assignment semantics; #18477 supplies the shipped example.
- The existing learning tree has DockLayouts and DockLayoutsAdoption under learn/guides/uibuildingblocks. DockZoneModel is technical reference under learn/agentos.
- learn/tree.json is navigation input; buildScripts/docs/seo/generate.mjs PRIORITIES is the ranking input. Generated portal sitemap/llms output is pipeline-owned.
- [ADR 0029](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/b537d0a3c8101c7d9fcb2a23317b6133d8d356ec/learn/agentos/decisions/0029-docking-design.md#L348) keeps pane components layout-blind. A beginner pane should be an ordinary component.

## The Fix

Create a first-layout tutorial under learn/guides/uibuildingblocks, choosing a clear non-duplicating title/path at intake and registering it in the source navigation and SEO-priority inputs.

Build and run the tutorial before writing the final prose. Start with an ordinary application/Workspace import, show a small complete panes/zones declaration, then explain what the reader sees and how to change one useful detail. Include at least a split, a tab group, an edge auto-hidden pane and an ordinary lazy module. Give complete run/navigation instructions and a link to the shipped runnable example; no omitted prerequisite should require private Discussion knowledge.

Explain generated structural IDs through the benefit of not maintaining them, not through an algorithm tutorial. Show a runtime move/rail reveal without changing the initial config. Briefly state that stage one is initial-only and persistence is not automatically enabled. Link to the adoption guide for computed/app integration and to the model/API reference for detailed grammar.

| Beginner instructions/snippets | Final #18476 API and #18477 example | A reader can create and run the shown standalone layout without internal hooks/imports | Errors and prerequisites explained from observed behavior | New first-layout tutorial | Reproduce the written steps in a fresh basic consumer |
| Navigation/discovery | learn/tree.json and SEO PRIORITIES | Guide is reachable from the learning navigation and related dock material | Broken links or missing registration fail this leaf | Source registration and cross-links | Rendered portal navigation/link checks |

## Discussion Criteria Mapping

Source criteria 1 and 4: a newcomer can discover, follow and run the basic stage-one declaration workflow without projection/resolver internals or private discussion history.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: Publish a complete first-layout walkthrough whose code and run steps execute against the shipped host. No custom constructor/resolver/cache/projection hook or private scratch import is required for its basic layout.
- [ ] AC-2: The written example visibly demonstrates its split, tabs, edge rail and lazy pane. Execute the stated interaction steps and show the observed result, rather than deriving the screenshot or claim from model JSON.
- [ ] AC-3: Explain initial config versus runtime operations and the stage-one persistence limit accurately, without teaching proposed persistence/workspaces/bound-panes APIs.
- [ ] AC-4: Register the new guide in learn/tree.json and SEO PRIORITIES; link it from the existing dock learning path and to the adoption/reference material. Keep publication links usable even if the parallel adoption rewrite has not landed yet.
- [ ] AC-5: Render-verify the complete guide, code blocks, diagram and links in the actual portal. Follow guide-authoring's grounding and reader-benefit bar; avoid an API-table dump or internal development narrative.
- [ ] AC-6: Do not edit or generate-and-commit apps/portal/sitemap.xml or apps/portal/llms.txt. The guide contains no ticket/PR archaeology or client-specific examples.

## Validation

Use the shipped example's normal run path:

    npm run server-start -- --port <free-port> --no-open

Open the documented example and the portal guide from the same checkout. The PR records the exact head, successful step-by-step run, rendered diagram/code/navigation checks and links followed. Run available source navigation/guide checks through their canonical owner; verify the actual script exists before naming its invocation. A generic unit-test pass is not tutorial usability evidence.

## Dependencies and Decision Record

Native blocked-by dependencies: #18476 and #18477. Both APIs and the runnable example must exist before this tutorial can be accepted; drafting preparation may proceed independently.

Decision Record: REQUIRED at the parent capability; the normative ADR amendment is delivered by #18476.

Decision Record impact: aligned-with the host's ADR 0029 amendment. No authority change; explanations link to the committed reference.

## Out of Scope

API implementation, example refactoring, exhaustive configuration reference, broad adoption/migration guidance, persistence, multi-window or reactive-pane features.

## Avoided Traps

No source-only proof of a runnable tutorial; no copy of the advanced demo presented as a beginner recipe; no generated output commits; no duplicated configuration catalog.
